name: Kolar Gold Fields (KGF)
description: One of the deepest gold mines in the world (over 3,000 meters / Champion Reef mine). Produced gold for over a century before closing in 2001.
examFacts: Second deepest underground mine in the world at its peak (~3.2 km deep Champion Reef mine).
Electrified in 1902 using power from the Shivanasamudra Hydroelectric Project (Asia's first major hydroelectric plant).
Operated by Bharat Gold Mines Limited (BGML) before operations halted in 2001 due to declining ore grade.

name: Panna Diamond Belt (Majhgawan)
description: Only active, mechanized commercial diamond mining region in India, operated by NMDC.
examFacts: India's sole active commercial diamond mine, hosted in Proterozoic kimberlite/lamproite pipes and alluvial gravels.
Operated by National Mineral Development Corporation (NMDC) with an annual capacity of ~84,000 carats.
Located in the Vindhyan Supergroup geological formation adjacent to the Ken River.

name: Jharia Coalfield
description: Largest repository of prime metallurgical coking coal in India, famous for long-burning underground mine fires.
examFacts: India's richest source of metallurgical coking coal required for blast furnace steel production.
Part of the Damodar Valley Gondwana coal belt (along with Raniganj, Bokaro, and Karanpura).
Famous for uncontrolled underground coal seam fires burning continuously since 1916.

name: Singhbhum Copper Belt
description: Prominent mineralized shear zone hosting copper mines (Mosabani, Rakha) and uranium deposits (Jaduguda).
examFacts: Singhbhum Shear Zone (SSZ) is an arcuate thrust belt separating the Singhbhum Craton from the North Singhbhum Fold Belt.
Hosts Jaduguda, India's first commercial uranium mine operated by Uranium Corporation of India Limited (UCIL).
Hindustan Copper Limited (HCL) operates the Indian Copper Complex at Ghatsila here.

name: Kudremukh Iron Ore Deposit
description: High-grade magnetite deposit in the Western Ghats. Mining ceased after Supreme Court environmental rulings.
examFacts: Name literally means 'Horse Face' due to the distinctive shape of the peak.
Mining was completely halted in 2005 by the Supreme Court to preserve the fragile biodiversity of Kudremukh National Park.
Pioneered the slurry pipeline method to transport iron ore concentrate 110 km to Mangalore Port.

name: Bailadila Iron Ore Range
description: One of the world's richest hematite deposits with over 65% iron content, operated by NMDC.
examFacts: Name 'Bailadila' translates to 'Bullock's Hump' in the local dialect due to the shape of the mountain ridge.
High-grade blue dust and lump ore is exported to Japan and domestic steel plants via Visakhapatnam Port.
Connected via the KK (Kottavalasa-Kirandul) railway line, India's highest broad-gauge railway line passing through the Eastern Ghats.

name: Khetri Copper Complex
description: Ancient and modern copper belt along the Aravalli Range; mined since the Indus Valley and Harappan eras.
examFacts: Mining history dates back 4,000+ years to the Harappan and Vedic periods (Ganeshwar-Jodhpura culture).
Operated by Hindustan Copper Limited (HCL); prominent mines include Khetri, Kolihan, and Chandmari.
Associated with the North Delhi Fold Belt of the Aravalli mountain chain.

name: Bombay High (Mumbai High)
district: Offshore Arabian Sea (160 km west of Mumbai)
description: India's most productive offshore oil and gas field, discovered in 1974 and operated by ONGC.
examFacts: Discovered in February 1974 by the Russian-Indian seismic exploration vessel and drillship Sagar Samrat.
Operated by Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC); yields sweet crude oil with low sulfur content.
Crude is transported via submarine pipelines to Uran processing plant on the mainland.

name: Digboi Oilfield
description: Birthplace of the oil industry in India and Asia; oil discovered in 1889; Digboi Refinery established in 1901.
examFacts: Asia's first oil well was drilled here in 1889; Digboi Refinery (commissioned in 1901) is the world's oldest continuously operating oil refinery.
Historically operated by the Assam Oil Company, now managed by Indian Oil Corporation (IOCL).
Legend states the British engineer cried 'Dig boy, dig!' to the laborers, giving the town its historic name.

name: Panchpatmali Bauxite Deposit
description: Asia's largest opencast bauxite mine, feeding the National Aluminium Company (NALCO) refinery at Damanjodi.
examFacts: Odisha accounts for more than 50% of India's total bauxite production and reserves.
Captive mine for NALCO; ore is transported down the mountain via a 14.6 km long single-flight curved overland conveyor belt.
Bauxite occurs as lateritic cappings on high-altitude Eastern Ghats plateaus (Panchpatmali, Baphlimali).
